title: Arlington
name: Arlington
metaTitle: Arlington 1031 Exchange Services in Jacksonville, FL
metaDescription: Arlington 1031 exchange coordination for value-add retail and flex-industrial replacement property near Regency Square and Monument Road.

sections.html:
Arlington sits east of downtown across the St. Johns River, reached by the Mathews and Hart bridges, and the replacement-property scope here is defined by asset age rather than a single dominant use: older strip retail, flex-industrial near Monument Road, and a regional mall corridor at Regency Square carrying more redevelopment potential than stabilized income.

A submittal package for Arlington should lead with a capital-needs assessment rather than a standard rent roll, since the corridor's building age makes deferred capital the more decision-relevant number for most qualifying properties.

sections.heading: Value-Add Scope Around Regency Square
sections.html:
Regency Square and the surrounding Arlington Expressway frontage include retail buildings from several development eras, and a meaningful share of the qualifying inventory in this corridor trades on a value-add basis rather than as stabilized net-lease product. Buyers coming into Arlington for a 1031 exchange are more often underwriting a repositioning story, backfilling vacancy or converting obsolete big-box space, than buying a fully leased asset outright.

University of North Florida and the nearby community college campus contribute a secondary, education-adjacent demand pool for smaller retail and service tenants, though that draw supplements rather than replaces the corridor's broader value-add character.

sections.heading: Property Types
sections.html:
Arlington's identification lists typically draw from the following categories:

  • older strip retail along the Arlington Expressway
  • flex-industrial and small-bay warehouse near Monument Road
  • single-tenant retail pads with near-term lease rollover
  • self-storage conversions of former retail buildings
  • light-industrial land near the river for eventual redevelopment

Pricing across these categories tends to reflect the capital-improvement burden attached to each specific building rather than a uniform per-square-foot benchmark, so comparable sales in this corridor should be adjusted for condition before being applied to a target property.

sections.heading: Arlington Expressway and Monument Road Corridor Specifications
sections.html:
The Arlington Expressway (State Road 115) functions as the primary retail spine, while Monument Road carries the corridor's flex and small-bay industrial stock, much of it developed decades ago for uses that have since changed hands multiple times. Building specifications on the Monument Road stock should be verified against current use rather than assumed from the original permit, since clear heights and dock configurations vary widely building to building in this older inventory.

Rail spurs along portions of Monument Road, remnants of the corridor's earlier industrial development, should be confirmed as active or abandoned before a buyer represents rail access as a current property feature.

sections.heading: Redevelopment and Reuse Diligence Items
sections.html:
Roof age, HVAC system condition, and electrical service capacity should be documented independently on any Arlington acquisition, since the corridor's older building stock means deferred maintenance is a common source of underwriting surprises. Any property near Regency Square should be reviewed against current mall-anchor occupancy, since anchor vacancy at the regional center affects surrounding outparcel and strip-retail traffic more than most single-property underwriting accounts for.

Environmental Phase I review is worth prioritizing on older Arlington industrial and flex parcels given the corridor's manufacturing history, and any recognized environmental condition flagged in that report should be resolved or priced before the property is carried on a final identification list.

sections.heading: Sequencing for Older Asset Stock
sections.html:
Because much of Arlington's qualifying inventory requires a capital-improvement plan rather than a simple hold, exchangers should have contractor bids and a scope-of-work estimate ready alongside the standard identification paperwork, since a lender evaluating an older building will generally want to see a capital plan before committing to a term sheet. Coordination with the qualified intermediary should account for the extra time a value-add underwriting package takes to assemble.

Buyers should also confirm current zoning entitlements before assuming a redevelopment or reuse plan is permissible as-of-right, since parcels near Regency Square carry a mix of legacy commercial and mixed-use zoning that has not been uniformly updated across the corridor.

faqs.q: Is most Arlington replacement property stabilized or value-add?
faqs.a: Value-add is more common. A meaningful share of the qualifying inventory near Regency Square and the Arlington Expressway trades on a repositioning basis rather than as fully leased, stabilized product, and buyers should expect to underwrite a lease-up or renovation timeline rather than day-one stabilized income.

faqs.q: What building specifications need independent verification in Arlington?
faqs.a: Roof age, HVAC condition, and electrical service capacity on older strip retail and flex-industrial stock, since the corridor's building age makes deferred maintenance a common source of underwriting surprises.

faqs.q: How does Regency Square's anchor occupancy affect nearby outparcels?
faqs.a: Anchor vacancy at the regional mall reduces foot traffic for surrounding strip retail and outparcels more than isolated property-level underwriting typically accounts for, so current anchor status should be confirmed before identification.

faqs.q: What should a lender see before financing an Arlington value-add property?
faqs.a: A capital-improvement plan with contractor bids and a scope-of-work estimate, since lenders evaluating older Arlington building stock generally want that documentation before committing to a term sheet, and a realistic contingency line should be built into the budget given the corridor's building age.

faqs.q: What kind of industrial stock is available near Monument Road?
faqs.a: Older flex and small-bay industrial buildings, originally built for a range of uses, with clear heights and dock configurations that vary considerably and should be verified against current condition rather than the original permit. Several parcels also carry remnant rail infrastructure that should be confirmed as active or abandoned before it is represented as a property feature, and a buyer should request that confirmation in writing rather than accept a verbal assurance from a listing broker.
